description:
One shared fixture builds a repository whose configuration declares a type hierarchy and the namespaces tests assert on, so no test has to depend on the binary supplying either.

## Background

Sixty-four call sites across the workspace construct a repository through the scaffold's default hierarchy template and then assert on the type names it wrote. Those assertions hold only because the binary supplies a taxonomy, and it is about to stop.

One fixture replaces that dependency, and it is authored once. The shared test-utility module is where the crate's suites already reach for repository setup, so it goes there and every other suite consumes it — a fixture per module family would satisfy the sizing of the adoptions while producing the near-duplicate setup the shared-contract rule exists to prevent.

Its vocabulary is the suite's own, chosen for the assertions that read it, and deliberately not a copy of what any package declares: a test asserting that a strategic type resolves is testing the mechanism, not the vocabulary.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One fixture in the shared test-utility module builds a repository whose configuration declares a type hierarchy, its label associations, and the namespaces its consumers assert on.
- [hard] REQ-02: The fixture declares that vocabulary in the test rather than reading it from any shipped default, so it holds whether or not the binary supplies one.
- [hard] REQ-03: The fixture exposes the vocabulary it declared, so a consumer asserts against what it was given rather than against a literal it repeats.
- [hard] REQ-04: Its own assertions establish that a repository built through it carries exactly the declared hierarchy and namespaces.
- [hard] REQ-05: No existing test changes here; adoption is separate work.

## Notes

Every adoption entry consumes this fixture as authored. If one needs a different vocabulary, it declares that beside its own assertions rather than adding a second fixture.
title: Author a test fixture that declares its own taxonomy
